scenes.headline: How to change a model by deleting weights
scenes.sub: And by solving one matrix in closed form
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Fennimore! Two ways to teach a language model a skill without ordinary fine-tuning. One deletes weights. The other solves one matrix.

scenes.text: Keep every pretrained weight. Learn only which gate weights to set to zero, and ship that choice as a bitmask.
scenes.mark: which gate weights to set to zero
scenes.say: Deletion Tuning keeps every pretrained weight, and learns only which gate weights to set to zero.

steps.say: Freeze a pretrained model. The target is one matrix per block, the MLP's gate projection.
Every gate weight gets a logit. A steep sigmoid of it multiplies the weight, so the weight is kept or nearly zero.
The usual loss, from reinforcement learning or labels, sends gradients only to the logits. The weights never change.
The sigmoid sharpens into a step. What ships is one bit per weight.

parts.note: what 256 neurons see, and what the teacher wants
parts.say: The second post picks two hundred fifty-six neurons in a late MLP. Keys are what they see at the answer; values are what a teacher wants.
This term protects ordinary text. Without it, the solve wrecks the model.

parts.say: One solve, about three milliseconds, writes the decision into one matrix.
